name: Slint
label: Touch and Go
lede: Four Louisville kids named their band after a pet fish, broke up before their second album came out, never toured it, and watched it sell year after year to people who swear it changed how rock could sound.

eras.title: Named after a pet fish
eras.text: Britt Walford and Brian McMahan had played together since middle school at Louisville's Brown School, then in Squirrel Bait. Walford and David Pajo came out of the prog-punk band Maurice, whose last songs became Slint's first. They wanted a heavier, stranger band, and Big Black and the Minutemen showed them how.

years.h: Britt Walford and Brian McMahan: Languid and Flaccid to Squirrel Bait
years.p: Walford and McMahan play in middle school as Languid and Flaccid with [[Ned Oldham|57b40135-dad3-4514-9e28-fc446cf20585]], then in [[Squirrel Bait|5dbf117b-c076-4d3b-b7ae-13517c25b2cf]]. Walford and David Pajo's band Maurice falls apart as they chase a [[Minutemen|d4ad0149-d8ae-4105-8009-0221fce9ff35]]-style sound.

years.h: First show: a Unitarian church empties in two songs
years.p: Britt Walford, David Pajo and 18-year-old bassist Ethan Buckler play for a Unitarian Universalist congregation as Small Tight Dirty Tufts of Hair. Most of the audience leaves during the first two songs.

years.h: Brian McMahan joins, and the band becomes Slint
years.p: Brian McMahan joins on guitar and the band renames itself Slint, after Britt Walford's pet fish.

years.h: Slint records Tweez with Steve Albini, and spills tea on his desk
years.p: Slint picks [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]] because of [[Big Black|9463868f-edc8-427e-ac07-ea89698e5f15]]. At mixdown Britt Walford asks for a bass drum like a ham slapped by a catcher's mitt, then spills tea on Albini's mixing board.
years.xp: Most of the words were made up in the studio; the band left in ad-libbed talk and sound effects between songs. Eight of the nine tracks are named after band members' parents, and the ninth, Rhoda, after Walford's dog.

years.h: Ethan Buckler quits and starts King Kong
years.p: Unhappy with the Tweez sessions, bassist Ethan Buckler leaves and forms [[King Kong|fd95f811-981e-4802-a712-f023fc4197fb]], which at first includes all the Slint members on different instruments.

eras.title: The record a friend paid for
eras.text: Touch and Go didn't answer, so a friend put up the money for Tweez. By the time it came out, most of Slint was in college, coming home on breaks to rehearse in the Walfords' basement, repeating riffs until they changed shape.

years.h: Todd Brashear joins Slint on bass
years.p: Todd Brashear takes over bass from Ethan Buckler and stays through Spiderland.

years.h: Tweez, on a label named after the friend who paid
years.p: When Touch and Go didn't respond, Slint's friend Jennifer Hartman paid to press Tweez. It came out in a tiny run as the only release on Jennifer Hartman Records.

eras.title: Four days in Chicago
eras.text: Slint wrote Spiderland slowly and recorded it fast with Brian Paulson, then stopped being a band before it came out. No tour, no interviews, no photo shoot, no video. Brian McMahan had nearly died on the road that year, and the record carries it.

years.h: Britt Walford drums on The Breeders' Pod as Shannon Doughton
years.p: Slint's drummer plays on [[The Breeders|667e856e-f3a7-42e9-8244-95422ef31321]]' debut Pod, recorded by [[Steve Albini|a4d486bd-6020-4a36-9c7d-bf5ce174bcd1]], under the name Shannon Doughton. On the Safari EP he's credited as Mike Hunt.

years.h: Brian McMahan's near-fatal car crash on the way to Bastro
years.p: Driving to see Brian Paulson record [[Bastro|cfc5b1bf-a46c-4504-bcb6-a820416a1894]], Brian McMahan is in a near-fatal crash. A paramedic calls in Code 138, and McMahan comes to singing the [[Misfits|936addc3-91aa-49de-8ec0-0dc186de151f]]' We Are 138.
years.xp: Wikipedia says the crash deeply affected McMahan and shaped the Spiderland sessions. He had worked out his vocals at home on a four-track, sitting in his parents' car to get the quiet spoken parts right over loud instruments.

years.h: Spiderland recorded in four days at River North, Chicago
years.p: Brian Paulson records Slint live at River North in Chicago, with vocals overdubbed in two takes or fewer. One microphone for the whispered parts, one for the screamed ones, and no added effects in the mix.

years.h: Will Oldham shoots the Spiderland cover in an Indiana quarry
years.p: Longtime friend [[Will Oldham|eb51090c-662a-47a1-967c-c63292d9831a]] photographs the band in an abandoned quarry in Utica, Indiana. The chosen shot is just four heads above the water.

years.h: Slint breaks up before Spiderland comes out
years.p: Slint ends in November 1990. According to Wikipedia, the story told since is that Brian McMahan checked himself into a hospital right after the sessions and was treated for depression.

years.h: Spiderland · Touch and Go
years.p: Six songs, from Breadcrumb Trail to Good Morning, Captain, David Pajo's favorite. The sleeve carries an ad inviting female vocalists to write to a Louisville address; [[PJ Harvey|e795e03d-b5d5-4a5f-834d-162cfb308a2c]] was among those who answered.
years.xp: Don, Aman is an anagram of Madonna, Nosferatu Man takes off from the 1922 film, and the instrumental For Dinner... uses no pedals at all. Wikipedia says the first year's sales were only a few thousand.

q: In 10 years it will be a landmark
years.h: Steve Albini's Melody Maker review predicts a landmark
years.p: Reviewing Spiderland in Melody Maker, Steve Albini tells readers to buy it now before they have to scramble for it.

eras.title: Everybody else's band
eras.text: Slint didn't exist, but Spiderland kept selling several thousand copies a year, according to Breadcrumb Trail, a feat for an indie record by a dead band. Its whisper-to-scream shape turned into a genre, and the members turned up all over it.

years.h: Touch and Go reissues Tweez
years.p: Touch and Go puts Slint's debut Tweez, first issued on Jennifer Hartman Records, back in print.

years.h: Untitled 10": two lost Albini tracks, Glenn and Rhoda
years.p: In 1989 Slint cut two instrumentals with Steve Albini for a 12-inch on Jennifer Hartman Records, then shelved them when Touch and Go's [[Corey Rusk|7e85d4b9-f01b-4d5f-892b-523daae2917c]] got interested. Five years later they come out: Glenn and a new Rhoda.

years.h: Brian McMahan forms the For Carnation; David Pajo joins Tortoise
years.p: McMahan starts [[The For Carnation|f3b9bb88-e82a-44e0-9f81-ae3acd4f8436]]. Pajo plays with [[Tortoise|e0953daa-860f-4dc8-9f1a-b12587cdaf17]], [[Palace|44d766e3-fc4a-4c19-9cdc-cd69966de1d8]] and later as [[Papa M|6edbe0fb-734e-4b1d-9c64-73ebb04853e1]], [[Zwan|5af2629b-36de-486c-ad50-a89a28ff050f]] and [[Interpol|b23e8a63-8f47-4882-b55b-df2c92ef400e]]. Walford plays in Evergreen.

eras.title: Playing it back
eras.text: Nearly fifteen years on, Slint came back on its own terms: short runs, no new album, Spiderland played in full. A box set and a documentary closed the book, and the band called it done.

years.h: Slint's first shows in 15 years, curating ATP
years.p: Brian McMahan, David Pajo and Britt Walford curate All Tomorrow's Parties at Camber Sands, England, and play an 18-date tour, insisting it's a one-time thing.

years.h: Spiderland played in full, and a new song, King's Approach
years.p: Slint plays Spiderland start to finish at Primavera Sound, ATP's Don't Look Back and Chicago's Pitchfork festival, and debuts a new song, King's Approach. It has never been recorded.

years.h: Todd Brashear runs Louisville's Wild and Woolly Video
years.p: Former Slint bassist Todd Brashear is the owner of Wild and Woolly Video, a Louisville rental store that outlasted almost every other.

years.h: Slint headlines ATP's last Camber Sands festival
years.p: Slint returns to Camber Sands to headline the final All Tomorrow's Parties weekender there.

years.h: Spiderland box set and Lance Bangs' Breadcrumb Trail
years.p: Touch and Go's remastered box adds 1989–90 live, demo and practice tapes and Breadcrumb Trail, Lance Bangs' 90-minute film shot over 12 years. Metacritic scores it 99.

years.h: Primavera and Green Man, then Slint stops again
years.p: After Primavera Sound in Spain and Portugal and Green Man in Wales, Slint disbands with no plans for new material.

years.h: David Pajo survives a suicide attempt
years.p: David Pajo attempts suicide after posting a long note on his blog, Wikipedia reports. He survived, and Uncut and Vice reported him recovering.

sources.title: Louisville Public Media: Off the Record, Todd Brashear
